title: Verifier-Guided Bounded Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered Paired Study under Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of permitting a single verifier-triggered automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling). Provider-call reconciliation shows 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Baseline configurations passed the deterministic verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline (validate → ≤1 repair) passed 200/200 (100%). Paired contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p (exact-binomial two-sided convention) = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.00, 0.015]. The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence/ordering breach in an extreme multi-step task. We report the preregistration, complete execution accounting, paired analysis, representative diagnostics for the repaired pair, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to synthesize device configurations from high-level operator intent for network operations (NetOps). For operational adoption, generators must satisfy deterministic invariants (ordering/workflow constraints, group-level safety, reachability, and policy compliance). A natural architectural response is a guarded pipeline that validates generated artifacts and, when possible, performs bounded automated repairs (generate → validate → repair). Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility for intent→configuration translation [1], and deterministic configuration verifiers provide an operational oracle appropriate for evaluating generated network artifacts [2]. However, an open empirical question remains: when the identical generated candidate is reused across comparison arms, what marginal effect does a verifier-triggered bounded repair actually produce? Put differently, if baseline (single-shot generation) and guarded conditions start from the exact same initial candidate per task, any paired difference must arise solely from the permitted validator-triggered repair, not from independent guarded first-pass generations or multi-sample selection.

This paper reports a preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) designed to isolate that repair-only estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We executed 200 deterministic tasks using a deterministic task generator and a deterministic verifier and examined whether a single validator-triggered repair invocation (≤1 repair) can change the per-task binary verifier outcome. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment with complete execution accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis showing baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0); (3) diagnostic evidence from archived validator traces explaining the single repaired pair; and (4) a focused discussion of inference limits and operationally bounded conclusions given the observed ceiling performance.
sections.related_work:
Three streams in the verified literature motivated our design. First, intent→configuration pipelines and benchmark efforts demonstrate that LLMs can produce device configurations from natural-language intent and that task banks/benchmarks exist to probe this capability [1]. Those works primarily present prototypes and dataset-limited evaluations rather than large-scale production deployments, which informed our use of a synthetic deterministic task bank to exercise complex, stress-oriented workflows. Second, deterministic configuration verification methods provide formal or operational oracles that check syntactic and semantic invariants (ordering, waypointing, isolation, group-level constraints) and have been applied to configuration validation and verification tasks; such verifiers are an appropriate oracle for correctness in generation→validation studies [2]. Third, generate→validate→repair and tool-augmented LLM agent designs have been proposed and demonstrated in adjacent domains (program repair, decompilation, model-based repair), showing that coupling generation with executable checks enables automated correction loops; these demonstrations motivate guarded NetOps pipelines but are primarily domain-adjacent evidence rather than direct NetOps empirical proof [4],[6],[?].

Synthesis and gap. The verified literature supports prototype intent→config systems [1], the use of deterministic verifiers as operational oracles [2], and the conceptual promise of generate→validate→repair loops in other domains. What remains underexplored—and what we address—is the narrow, experimentally controlled question: when baseline and guarded conditions reuse the identical initial candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate), what marginal improvement can a bounded, verifier-triggered repair produce? Prior demonstrations often conflate repair with independent guarded resampling or constrained prompting; our paired, shared-initial design isolates repair-only effects.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (CAND-2026-001) fixed a paired binary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, comparing per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance for baseline (single-shot initial generation without repair) versus guarded (same initial candidate, verifier may trigger ≤1 repair). The preregistration fixed N=200 tasks, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both episodes), and a maximum of one automated repair call per task. Primary analysis used exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial two-sided convention) on discordant counts and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration also recorded a sensitivity plan treating persistent unparsables as failures; all preregistered settings and the analysis executor are archived.

Deterministic task bank and verifier oracle. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected via a fixed index rule; each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The operational oracle, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, parses generated commands, enforces allowed_touched_fields and workflow ordering (required_sequence), evaluates group constraints and minimum-active invariants, and emits structured tracer output that deterministically determines the binary per-episode score (full_intent_constraint_validation). Validator tracer outputs (validation_before and validation_after) are archived and constitute the authoritative evidence for scoring and failure diagnosis.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics, sanitizer, and repair policy. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the same single sampled candidate was supplied to both baseline and guarded episodes. Consequently, any paired difference can arise only from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. Before verifier parsing a deterministic formatting sanitizer ran; if the verifier reported invariant violations the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call with a repair prompt constructed from the validator trace. Repair prompts and the single repair provider trace are archived. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property even though the experiment deterministically reused one initial sample per pair.

Provider-call accounting and statistical procedures. Deterministic reconciliation records: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, summing to hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. Primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar implemented via exact binomial-tail on discordant counts (n = n10 + n01, k = n10) as preregistered. For the paired absolute risk difference we computed the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; these bootstrap parameters are recorded and archived. The analysis executor's outputs (condition-level counts, contingency table, p-value, and CI) are reproduced by re-running the archived analysis executor on the raw results.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and timing. The run completed without preregistered exclusions or persistent unparsables. Provider-call reconciliation reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and cache_miss_count = 201 (no cache hits); elapsed runtime ≈29 minutes (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00). Pair accounting is consistent: complete_pairs = 200, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic verifier accepted baseline configurations in 199/200 tasks (baseline success_rate = 0.995) and guarded configurations in 200/200 tasks (guarded success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, yielding paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial two-sided convention) equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute risk difference is [0.00, 0.015]. All numbers and analysis artifacts are archived and reproduce from the recorded raw results.

Single repair event: diagnostic trace. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator traces for the repaired pair indicate the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint. The repaired task's difficulty metadata classify it as extreme (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme"). The validator's validation_before recorded violation codes documenting an ordering breach; after the bounded repair the validator's validation_after.valid = true and the scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". The archived repair provider trace shows that the repair produced a reordering of the sequenced commands; the verifier trace fields are the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered repair that enacted the required reordering.

Exploratory diagnostics and difficulty patterns. Representative task manifests and traces archived with the run show required_command_count spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count values up to 3 in the sampled very_hard / extreme task families. The lone baseline failure and the repaired pair are associated with extreme composite difficulty (high required_command_count and multiple changed interfaces), consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures under single-shot generation.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation given shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because each pair reuses the identical sampled candidate, observed paired differences isolate the marginal effect of permitting a single verifier-triggered repair; the experiment therefore measures a repair-only estimand. It does not measure effects that would arise from independent guarded first-pass sampling, constrained prompts, or selection among multiple candidates.

What the numeric results imply. The observed baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) produced a sparse-discordant inference regime: only one discordant pair (n = 1) implies the exact two-sided McNemar p-value conveys limited directional evidence (p = 1.0 under the exact-binomial two-sided convention), while the paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.015] bounds the plausible absolute improvement attributable to repair in this repair-only estimand. In practical terms, given the realized high baseline, the data are compatible with at most a small absolute improvement (≤1.5 percentage points) that could be attributed to a single bounded repair across the sampled tasks.

Failure-mode and task-difficulty interpretation. The single repaired pair arose in a task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3 (difficulty.level = "extreme"). Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a required_sequence/ordering violation; the bounded repair applied a reordering that satisfied the verifier's required_sequence constraints. Representative manifests and traces indicate that residual failures, when they occur, concentrate in tasks that require multi-step, cross-interface sequencing and where the workflow policy encodes nontrivial group constraints (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields). This pattern suggests a targeted operational hypothesis: bounded verifier-guided repairs are most likely to produce observable gains on complex sequencing/order faults that are expressible in the verifier's manifest-level invariants.

Statistical-power and ceiling effects. The preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N=200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%). The unexpectedly high baseline pass rate drastically reduces realized power for detecting small repair-only effects. The paired-bootstrap CI quantifies the limited uncertainty: although a nonzero repair-only effect is possible, the upper bound (0.015) is small in absolute terms for this experimental domain and design.

Operationally bounded implications. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair can correct certain ordering/dependency violations expressible in the manifest invariants. This is direct, narrow evidence for repair efficacy on that class of fault; it is not evidence that bounded repair would correct runtime dataplane omissions, remedy adversarially poisoned contexts, or generalize across models and heterogenous device families. Those broader claims require additional studies (multi-model sampling, independent guarded-first-pass designs, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

Threats to validity. Internal: the paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates repair effects but intentionally does not address prompt sensitivity or model-sampling variability. Recording temperature = null/unset does not establish deterministic sampling; the experiment's design used one initial sample per task but cannot assert that the hosted model's sampling behavior is deterministic. Construct: the deterministic verifier enforces manifest-encoded invariants but does not substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor runtime semantics. External: the single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini) on a synthetic deterministic task bank limits cross-model and production generality. Conclusion: with only one discordant pair statistical evidence for a nonzero repair-only effect is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI and archived diagnostic trace provide the transparent uncertainty and causal trace for the single observed repair.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (N=200) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline single-shot generations accepted by a deterministic verifier in 199/200 tasks, while the guarded pipeline (validate → ≤1 repair on the same initial candidate) accepted 200/200. Deterministic reconciliation records 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement is traced to a verifier-triggered reordering repair that corrected a required_sequence violation in an extreme multi-step task. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded bounded repair can remedy localized ordering/dependency faults that are expressible in manifest invariants in this synthetic verifier-backed setting. Broader operational claims require additional targeted experiments (multi-model designs, independent guarded first-pass sampling, adversarial contamination, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
